TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Tree Commission Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
5:30 PM, October 20, 2026 
 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2nd Floor Conference 
Room 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 The meeting was called to order by Chairman Commissioner Dr. M. Montgomery at 5:33 PM. 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 The Clerk called the roll, and the following members: 
Present  
Commissioner Dr. Michael Montgomery, Chair 
Commissioner Susan L. Neitlich 
Commissioner Diane E. Hoffman 
Commissioner Dr. Nathan Havill 
Commissioner Kyle Dougherty 
 
Also in attendance: Briana J. Belton-Robinson, Boards and Commissions Clerk. 
 
Roll Call Summary: Present, Voting: 5; Present, Not Voting: 0; Absent: 0; Excused: 0. 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 
 
  1. Regular Meeting of September 15th, 2026  
  Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery requested that approval of the September 15, 2026 
Regular Meeting Minutes be postponed until later in the meeting to allow the 
Commission to proceed with its scheduled business. 
 
The Commission subsequently reviewed the September 15, 2026 meeting minutes. 
 
The following correction was identified: 
 
• Under Reports – Tree Warden Report, the reference to Commissioner 
Hoffman as “S. Hoffman” was corrected to “D. Hoffman.” 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery also requested clarification regarding the spelling of
Earth Tones Native Plant Nursery. The committee confirmed that the name was 
recorded correctly and required no revision. 
 
A motion was made and seconded to approve the September 15, 2026, Regular 
Meeting Minutes as amended. The motion passed unanimously. 
 
A motion was made and seconded to approve the September 15, 2026, Regular 
Meeting Minutes as amended. The motion passed unanimously. 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
 There were no members of the public present in person or participating virtually. No public 
comments were received. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that correspondence received since the previous 
meeting primarily concerned matters within the Tree Warden's responsibilities. 
 
No additional correspondence requiring Commission action was presented. 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No Executive Session was held. 
7. REPORTS 
  
 
 
  1. Tree Warden Report (e.g., Removals, Postings, Permits)  
  Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery presented an update on behalf of Tree Warden 
Christopher Rhone. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that two trees located at 27 Barrett Street were 
the subject of a scheduled tree hearing on October 28, 2026, at noon. One tree was 
proposed for pruning, while the other was proposed for removal. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery also reported that fall tree planting had begun after 
trees were delivered the previous Thursday. As of the meeting, 11 trees had been 
planted, with additional planting anticipated throughout the remainder of the week. 
 
The Commission discussed several planting-related challenges, including changes in 
resident preferences, restrictions associated with planting locations, and the need to 
identify alternative sites for trees that could not be planted as originally planned. 
 
The Commission also discussed the importance of watering newly planted trees.
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery said he would follow up with property owners on 
watering responsibilities and monitor soil moisture. 
  2. On-Call Arborist RFP  
  Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that the Town initially received one inquiry 
regarding the On-Call Arborist Request for Proposals (RFP). Following the inquiry, it 
was decided to extend the submission deadline by one week, establishing a new 
deadline of October 27, 2026, at noon. 
 
The RFP was advertised through the State of Connecticut's procurement website. 
 
Commissioner D. Hoffman inquired whether the Connecticut Tree Protective 
Association was aware of the posting and suggested notifying the organization to 
increase awareness among qualified arborists and encourage additional submissions. 
 
The Commission discussed the procurement process and the responsibilities of the 
Town's Purchasing Agent. Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery explained that only the 
Purchasing Agent would know how many bids were received before the deadline. 
 
The bids would be publicly opened on October 27, 2026, at noon, at which time the 
submitted bid amounts would be read aloud. 
 
Commissioners expressed interest in increasing awareness of the opportunity while 
maintaining an open and equitable bidding process. 
8. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  1. Tree for Communities Gant  
  Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery updated the board on the Trees for Communities Grant 
and ongoing efforts to expand tree planting throughout Hamden. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that 47 trees were planned for fall planting, 
exceeding his initial target of 46 trees. Commissioners also discussed the trees 
previously planted at the Keefe Community Center and progress toward the broader 
annual planting goal of about 60 trees. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery noted that some trees purchased for the program were 
smaller than expected, saving costs and leaving grant funds available for additional 
purchases. 
 
The Commission discussed the administrative and financial responsibilities associated 
with implementing the grant. 
 
Commissioners noted that, unlike some municipalities, including New Britain, Hamden 
does not have an independent fiduciary organization responsible for administering its 
tree planting program. As a result, the Commission must coordinate directly with Town 
departments on procurement, payments, contractors, and other grant-related 
activities.
The Commission also discussed continued public outreach. Residents participating in 
the program received informational handouts concerning tree planting and related 
responsibilities. 
  2. Fall Planting  
  The Commission discussed ongoing fall planting activities, volunteer coordination, 
equipment needs, contractor availability, and potential planting locations. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that several locations required additional 
coordination due to property restrictions, changes in resident preferences, and the 
size of trees being delivered. 
 
Housing Authority Planting 
 
The Commission discussed arranging assistance with planting trees at the Hamden 
Housing Authority. 
 
Two red maple trees were planned for the property, with the possibility of adding a 
third tree, a Showtime crabapple. 
 
Commissioners noted that the red maples had root balls weighing approximately 400 
pounds each and that approximately eight volunteers would be needed to move and 
plant the trees safely. 
 
The Commission discussed the possibility of hiring a registered arborist or contractor 
to complete the planting. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that contractors generally charge 
approximately $500 per tree for planting services. 
 
Commissioner S. Neitlich noted that contracting for three properties at approximately 
$500 per tree would result in an estimated expenditure of $1,500, remaining below the 
applicable purchasing threshold. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery indicated that approximately $2,000 was available 
within his spending authorization. 
 
The Commission discussed identifying a contractor already registered as a Town 
vendor to simplify the procurement process. 
 
Volunteer Planting Schedule 
 
The Commission discussed several potential planting dates, including October 24–25 
and October 31–November 1, for residents and volunteers assisting with plantings on 
private property. 
 
A volunteer planting event was tentatively scheduled for Sunday, November 1, 2026, 
at 10:00 AM, subject to volunteer availability and weather conditions. 
 
The Commission discussed establishing an alternate date in the event of rain.
Commissioner S. Neitlich agreed to inquire about volunteer availability through the 
Whitneyville group. 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty stated that he would reach out to his networks in New 
Haven to identify additional volunteers. 
 
Public Works was expected to deliver and position trees at the designated locations 
on the Friday preceding the planting event. 
 
Additional Planting Locations 
 
The Commission discussed several residential planting locations requiring 
coordination, including: 
 
63 Barrett Street 
 
47 Homeland Street, where the resident indicated that he would complete the planting 
independently 
 
North Lane 
 
Other residential and institutional properties identified through the program 
 
The Commission also discussed a proposed planting location associated with a law 
firm and additional locations where property access or resident preferences required 
clarification. 
 
Approximately nine trees were discussed in connection with one of the planned 
planting locations. 
 
The Commission reviewed options for relocating trees that could no longer be planted 
at their originally designated sites. 
 
Showtime Crab-apple and Redbud Trees 
 
The Commission discussed the availability of Showtime crab-apple and redbud trees. 
 
Commissioner S. Neitlich suggested that the available Showtime crabapple might be 
suitable for planting at Darius Boyce's residence. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery asked Commissioner S. Neitlich to contact the family to 
determine whether they would be interested in receiving the tree. 
 
The Commission also discussed alternative locations for trees that could not be 
accommodated at their originally designated planting sites. 
 
Planting Supplies and Equipment 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that the Commission had established a
standing order with Paradise Nurseries for mulch required under the Trees for 
Communities Grant. 
 
The Commission also discussed purchasing approximately 60 preformed tree guards 
from A.M. Leonard Horticultural Tool & Supply, at an estimated cost of $7 per guard. 
 
The Commission did not order additional tree watering bags for the winter season. 
 
Commissioners discussed the importance of protecting newly planted trees and 
coordinating watering responsibilities with participating residents. 
  3. DEEP Tour on October 5th  
  Commissioner S. Neitlich summarized the October 5, 2026 tour with representatives 
from the Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP). 
 
The tour highlighted urban forestry initiatives and tree planting projects in New Haven 
and Hamden. 
 
Commissioner S. Neitlich reported that the group visited Criscuolo Park in New 
Haven, where about five volunteers participated in the tour. 
 
Representatives from the Urban Resources Initiative (URI) discussed community-
based urban forestry efforts, including volunteer participation, tree planting, and long-
term maintenance. 
 
The group also visited a nearby elementary school, where students, faculty, and 
community partners helped redesign and landscape the school's entrance area to 
include trees and other plantings. 
 
The tour continued down lower Dixwell Avenue, where a planting crew worked on an 
initiative involving about 127 trees. 
 
Commissioner S. Neitlich discussed the extensive coordination and labor required to 
establish and maintain urban tree planting programs. 
 
Commissioner D. Hoffman expressed surprise at the labor-intensive process of 
watering newly planted trees in New Haven. 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty explained that watering procedures vary by planting site, 
including whether a hose connection is available or a watering truck must be used. 
 
DEEP representatives then traveled to Hamden to observe the Town's tree-planting 
initiatives, including trees planted near the Keefe Community Center. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery provided information regarding Hamden's program, 
while Commissioner S. Neitlich discussed community outreach and volunteer 
participation. 
 
Commissioner S. Neitlich reported that the Hamden group received considerable 
praise for its efforts to establish and implement tree planting programs.
The Commission discussed the importance of continued collaboration with DEEP and 
other municipalities to strengthen Hamden's urban forestry initiatives. 
  4. WTHN Interview  
  IThe Commission discussed a recent WTNH News 8 segment highlighting Hamden's 
neighborhood tree planting program. 
 
Commissioner S. Neitlich reported that the interview was arranged following a 
recommendation to a WTNH reporter interested in featuring positive community 
initiatives. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery and Commissioner S. Neitlich participated in the 
interview, which also featured a local resident and her son. 
 
The segment highlighted tree planting efforts supported by the Trees for Communities 
program and previous Community Development Block Grant funding. 
 
The report described portions of Hamden as a "tree desert," emphasizing the limited 
number of existing street trees and opportunities to expand the Town's tree canopy. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that he identified about 45 vacant tree-planting 
locations in the neighborhood highlighted during the segment. 
 
Commissioners thanked the news coverage and discussed its potential to raise public 
awareness and encourage residents to participate in future planting initiatives. 
 
WTNH News 8: More Than 100 Trees Planted Through Hamden Neighborhood 
Program 
https://www.wtnh.com/news/connecticut/new-haven/more-than-100-trees-planted-
through-hamden-neighborhood-program/ 
  5. Tree Inventory  
  Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery provided an update on the proposed tree inventory 
initiative. 
 
The Commission discussed the State's interest in making tree inventory software 
available to the Town through a leasing arrangement. 
 
The Commission also discussed the existing inventory system and the need to 
coordinate with Town personnel to determine how to collect and incorporate additional 
tree data. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery indicated that he would follow up with Les Welker 
regarding the inventory system and available software options. 
 
The Commission discussed beginning its inventory work along Swarthmore Street, 
where mature pin oak trees have been the subject of ongoing concern. 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty was identified to assist with inventorying the trees along 
Swarthmore Street, including counting and measuring the trees.
Commissioners noted that some of the mature pin oaks could potentially qualify for 
inclusion in a notable tree inventory. 
 
The Commission emphasized that the initial inventory would focus on documenting 
tree locations, species, and measurements rather than conducting formal tree risk 
assessments. 
9. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  1. Swarthmore Street Pin Oak Trees  
  Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that residents of Swarthmore Street had met 
with the Mayor regarding concerns about the mature pin oak trees located along the 
street. 
 
Residents expressed a desire for the Town to take action to address their concerns. 
 
The Commission discussed the importance of establishing an accurate inventory of 
the trees before determining appropriate management recommendations. 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty will assist with counting and measuring the trees along 
Swarthmore Street. 
 
The Commission discussed documenting the number, size, and location of the trees 
to provide baseline information for further evaluation. 
 
Commissioners also noted that one or more of the mature pin oaks might qualify for 
recognition as notable trees. 
 
No formal action was taken. 
  2. Approval of 2027 Meeting Calendar  
  Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery presented the proposed 2027 Tree Commission 
meeting calendar. 
 
The Commission discussed continuing its regular meeting schedule on the third 
Tuesday of each month at 5:30 PM in the 2nd Floor Conference Room of the Hamden 
Government Center. 
 
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery moved to approve the proposed 2027 Tree 
Commission meeting calendar. Commissioner D. Hoffman seconded the motion. 
 
The Clerk took the following vote: 
Yes 
Commissioner Dr. Michael Montgomery, Chair 
Commissioner Susan L. Neitlich 
Commissioner Diane E. Hoffman 
Commissioner Dr. Nathan Havill 
Commissioner Kyle Dougherty
No 
 
The motion passed unanimously. 
 
Vote Summary: Yes 5, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 0 
10. ANNOUCEMENTS 
  
 Hamden Land Conservation Trust Presentation 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty reported that he had confirmed arrangements with Gail 
Cameron and the Hamden Land Conservation Trust (HLCT) to present a program titled 
"Notable Trees of Hamden." 
 
The presentation is scheduled for Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 7:00 PM, in the 
meeting space behind the Miller Memorial Library. 
 
Commissioner K. Dougherty will deliver the presentation, which will explore the history of 
notable trees throughout Connecticut before focusing specifically on notable trees in 
Hamden. 
 
The Commission discussed promoting the event to encourage public attendance. 
 
Upcoming Educational Conferences 
 
Commissioner D. Hoffman informed the Commission of two upcoming educational 
conferences and agreed to email informational flyers. 
 
2026 SALT Conference – Connecticut College 
 
Commissioner D. Hoffman announced that the 2026 SALT Conference would be held on 
Saturday, November 7, 2026, from 9:30 AM to 3:30 PM, at the Cummings Art Center at 
Connecticut College. Registration and a continental breakfast will begin at 8:30 AM. 
 
The conference will focus on ecological and landscape design considerations for transition 
zones between cultivated landscapes and natural forested areas. We will emphasize the 
strategic use of native understory trees and shrubs to enhance landscape functionality, 
seasonal interest, and habitat for native pollinators and wildlife. 
 
The conference will feature three educational sessions: 
 
Edgy Ecology for the Formal Forest Fringe – Presented by Lea Johnson, Ph.D., Director of 
Conservation at Native Plant Trust. This session explores ecological principles for plant 
selection and landscape design, including edge effects, patch size, light dynamics, shrub 
ecology, bird dispersal, and woodland garden design. 
 
Designing the Edge – Presented by Kate Cholakis, Professor of Landscape Planning and 
Design at the Conway School of Landscape Design. This presentation will examine the 
opportunities and challenges associated with the transition between managed landscapes
and natural ecosystems, emphasizing ecological design strategies and approaches to 
creating more dynamic landscape environments. 
 
Shrubs for the Forest Edge – Presented by Bryan Connolly, Ph.D., Associate Professor of 
Biology at Eastern Connecticut State University. This session highlights native shrubs and 
multi-stemmed woody plants for southern New England woodland gardens, including their 
horticultural characteristics, preferred growing conditions, ecological relationships, and 
available cultivars. 
 
The full-day conference will include a continental breakfast, three presentations, lunch, a 
panel discussion, and an optional post-conference tour. 
 
Registration is required, with a general admission fee of $75 and a discounted rate of $60 
for current Connecticut College Arboretum and Wild Ones members. A limited number of 
sponsored or discounted registrations will be available to eligible students, nonprofit 
representatives, and emerging industry professionals. 
 
Additional information, speaker biographies, and registration details are available through 
the 2026 SALT Conference website and Conference Registration. 
 
Connecticut Association of Conservation and Inland Wetlands Commissions (CACIWC) – 
2026 Annual Meeting 
 
Commissioner D. Hoffman also announced the upcoming 2026 Annual Meeting of the 
Connecticut Association of Conservation and Inland Wetlands Commissions (CACIWC). 
 
The annual meeting provides educational and networking opportunities for municipal 
conservation and inland wetlands commissioners, environmental professionals, and 
individuals involved in land conservation and natural resource management. 
 
Commissioner D. Hoffman agreed to distribute informational flyers and registration details 
for both conferences to Commission members. 
 
Additional information: CACIWC 2026 Annual Meeting 
11. ADJOURNMENT 
  
 There being no further business, Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery asked whether there were any 
objections to adjournment. 
 
Hearing none, the meeting was adjourned at 6:37 PM.
